## Why it moved, and why this stub exists rather than a deleted file

Written here on 2026-09-08 as `fortkit-keku` by Emrith Cairnwright, Mayor of
Manyhalls, **about a tree this fort cannot read**. That constraint shaped the
whole document: no line numbers, no counts, and every factual claim tagged
`[MEASURED]` / `[REPORTED]` / `[UNKNOWN]` according to whether this seat had read
it directly, was relaying a seat who could, or was asking rather than asserting.

On 2026-09-10 the Overseer moved the fleet programme to Proofdelve entirely. A
spec describing a tree its holder cannot read is a defect the moment somebody who
CAN read that tree is available to hold it.

**The move was not a copy, and the difference is measurable.** Standing order 12
applied per hunk: the self-describing section became false on arrival and was
rewritten, and every tag was re-evaluated by a seat for whom `[REPORTED]` means
something different. Measured across the two files on the day of the move:
`[REPORTED]` fell from **19 to 2**, `[UNKNOWN]` from 4 to 2, and the document grew
from 514 to 658 lines. **Seventeen relayed claims became measurements or
refutations.** That pass was worth more than the move.

This file is a stub rather than a deletion because a deleted path leaves a dead
link in every record that ever cited it — the beads, the handoffs, the Regent's
sittings and this fort's own annals all name `docs/specs/continuous-fleet.md`.
The superseded content is preserved in this repository's history; the last commit
carrying it whole is `6e79887`.

## What Manyhalls still owns here

The design record and nothing else. Improvements to the fleet reach this fort as
advisories under standing order 13, not as edits to this path. `fortkit-keku` is
closed against the receiving commit above.
